scope: Manual instruction-level evidence for initial VCS PSP versus VCS PS2 opcode review. Names are retained only when the bytecode behavior itself supports them.

slots.name: NOP
slots.finding: Both handlers are exactly `jr ra` with delay-slot `v0 = 0`. This is native VM dispatch status `CONTINUE`, not a script-level output; neither handler reads a parameter nor mutates thread state.

slots.name: WAIT
slots.finding: PS2 reads one script parameter, clears thread+0x20b, stores a derived wake value at thread+0x200 and reports native VM dispatch status 1 (`YIELD`). PSP enters its corresponding table target with the same one-parameter decoder setup, but its continuation lies outside the recovered PSP function boundary; no cross-platform semantic equality is claimed yet.

slots.name: GOTO
slots.finding: PS2 reads one script parameter and writes the resulting script position to thread+0x10 before reporting native VM dispatch status 0 (`CONTINUE`). PSP reaches the analogous table target with the same one-parameter decoder setup, but its continuation is outside the recovered PSP function boundary; no cross-platform semantic equality is claimed yet.

slots.name: SET_VAR_INT
slots.finding: PSP resolves a destination then collects one parameter; PS2 completes the direct raw-dword store. PSP post-collector continuation is outside its recovered boundary.

slots.name: SET_VAR_FLOAT
slots.finding: Shares the PSP/PS2 raw-dword assignment handler with 0004/0035/0036; PS2 directly stores the one collected raw parameter unchanged.

slots.name: SET_VAR_TEXT_LABEL
slots.finding: PSP resolves a destination and collects one parameter; PS2 directly stores that one raw dword. This is a duplicated native assignment target, not proof of a host-string ABI.

slots.name: ADD_VAL_TO_INT_VAR
slots.finding: PSP resolves destination and collects one parameter; PS2 directly writes destination + parameter with native 32-bit arithmetic. PSP post-collector continuation is outside its recovered boundary.

slots.name: ADD_VAL_TO_FLOAT_VAR
slots.finding: Both handlers resolve destination, collect one raw binary32 parameter, execute scalar float addition, store it and return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: SUB_VAL_FROM_INT_VAR
slots.finding: Both handlers resolve destination, collect one parameter, use native 32-bit subtraction and return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: SUB_VAL_FROM_FLOAT_VAR
slots.finding: Both handlers resolve destination, collect one raw binary32 parameter, execute scalar float subtraction, store it and return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: MULT_INT_VAR_BY_VAL
slots.finding: Both handlers resolve destination, collect one parameter, store the low 32 bits of native integer multiplication and return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: MULT_FLOAT_VAR_BY_VAL
slots.finding: Both handlers resolve destination, collect one raw binary32 parameter, execute scalar float multiplication, store it and return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: DIV_INT_VAR_BY_VAL
slots.finding: Both handlers issue native signed div/mflo after one-parameter collection and return status 0 for normal operands. The core faults explicitly for zero divisor and INT_MIN/-1 instead of inventing a hardware edge-case quotient.

slots.name: DIV_FLOAT_VAR_BY_VAL
slots.finding: Both handlers resolve destination, collect one raw binary32 parameter, execute scalar float division, store it and return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: IS_INT_VAR_GREATER_THAN_NUMBER
slots.finding: Both handlers collect two raw parameters, compute signed param[0] > param[1], XOR the result with thread+0x20c and apply the common +0x206/+0x209 condition reducer before returning native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: IS_NUMBER_GREATER_THAN_INT_VAR
slots.finding: Shares the complete PSP/PS2 signed param[0] > param[1] condition handler with 000F; source-kind notation is resolved before the handler sees the two raw parameters. It applies raw NOT, the common reducer and native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: IS_INT_VAR_GREATER_THAN_INT_VAR
slots.finding: Both dispatch tables target the already proved 000F/0010 signed param[0] > param[1] condition core; after two-parameter collection it applies raw NOT, the common reducer and native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: IS_FLOAT_VAR_GREATER_THAN_NUMBER
slots.finding: Both FPU handlers collect two raw binary32 parameters and implement the native branch predicate !(param[0] <= param[1]), then apply raw NOT, the common reducer and native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: IS_NUMBER_GREATER_THAN_FLOAT_VAR
slots.finding: Shares the complete PSP/PS2 float-greater native target with 0012; source-kind notation is resolved before the handler evaluates !(param[0] <= param[1]), raw NOT and the common reducer.

slots.name: IS_FLOAT_VAR_GREATER_THAN_FLOAT_VAR
slots.finding: Shares the complete PSP/PS2 float-greater native target with 0012; it evaluates !(param[0] <= param[1]), raw NOT and the common reducer before native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: IS_INT_VAR_GREATER_OR_EQUAL_TO_NUMBER
slots.finding: Both handlers collect two raw parameters, compute signed param[0] >= param[1], apply raw NOT and the common condition reducer, then return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: IS_NUMBER_GREATER_OR_EQUAL_TO_INT_VAR
slots.finding: Both dispatch tables target the already proved 0015 signed param[0] >= param[1] condition core; after two-parameter collection it applies raw NOT, the common reducer and native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: IS_INT_VAR_GREATER_OR_EQUAL_TO_INT_VAR
slots.finding: Both dispatch tables target the already proved 0015 signed param[0] >= param[1] condition core; after two-parameter collection it applies raw NOT, the common reducer and native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: IS_FLOAT_VAR_GREATER_OR_EQUAL_TO_NUMBER
slots.finding: Both FPU handlers collect two raw binary32 parameters and implement the native branch predicate !(param[0] < param[1]), then apply raw NOT, the common reducer and native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: IS_NUMBER_GREATER_OR_EQUAL_TO_FLOAT_VAR
slots.finding: Shares the complete PSP/PS2 float-greater-or-equal native target with 0018; source-kind notation is resolved before !(param[0] < param[1]), raw NOT and the common reducer.

slots.name: IS_FLOAT_VAR_GREATER_OR_EQUAL_TO_FLOAT_VAR
slots.finding: Shares the complete PSP/PS2 float-greater-or-equal native target with 0018; it evaluates !(param[0] < param[1]), raw NOT and the common reducer before native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: IS_INT_VAR_EQUAL_TO_NUMBER
slots.finding: Both handlers collect two raw parameters, compute param[0] == param[1], apply raw NOT and the common condition reducer, then return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: IS_INT_VAR_EQUAL_TO_INT_VAR
slots.finding: Both dispatch tables target the already proved 001B/02DB equality core; after two-parameter collection it applies raw NOT, the common reducer and native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: IS_FLOAT_VAR_EQUAL_TO_NUMBER
slots.finding: Both dispatch tables target the shared raw-dword equality core; despite the float spelling it compares the two collected 32-bit parameter patterns with XOR, then applies raw NOT, the common reducer and native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: IS_FLOAT_VAR_EQUAL_TO_FLOAT_VAR
slots.finding: Both dispatch tables target the shared raw-dword equality core; despite the float spelling it compares the two collected 32-bit parameter patterns with XOR, then applies raw NOT, the common reducer and native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: GOTO_IF_FALSE
slots.finding: PSP entry directly collects one parameter; PS2 proves that the decoded target replaces thread+0x10 only when thread+0x209 is false and returns native status 0 (`CONTINUE`). The PSP post-collector continuation is outside the recovered function boundary, so cross-platform equality is not claimed.

slots.name: START_NEW_SCRIPT
slots.finding: Both handlers collect one script index, clamp negative values to zero, call the platform script-thread factory, then collect exactly 0x60 raw parameters directly into child+0x54 and return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`). The factory/child lifetime is host-owned; the 96-local copy is VM semantics.

slots.name: GOSUB
slots.finding: PSP collects exactly one target parameter through confirmed CollectParameters; PS2 then visibly increments thread+0x204, stores the post-parameter IP at thread+0x14 + 4*old_depth without a function tag, resolves the script target and returns native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: RETURN
slots.finding: Both shared return cores decrement thread+0x204, restore thread+0x10 from thread+0x14 + 4*depth, and enter the richer output-copy path only for entries with bit 0x00800000. Thus tagless GOSUB frames return directly and tagged CALL/CALL_NOT frames share the separately proved function ABI; native status is 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: ADD_INT_VAR_TO_INT_VAR
slots.finding: Both tables share the 0007 native target: PSP has resolver/one-parameter collector setup and PS2 directly performs destination + parameter modulo 2^32.

slots.name: ARITHMETIC_DISPATCH_ALIAS_FLOAT_ADD
slots.finding: Both dispatch tables point 002A to the same direct PSP/PS2 float-add targets as 0008. The handler resolves a destination, collects one raw binary32 parameter, adds, stores and returns native status 0 (`CONTINUE`). The generic alias name intentionally does not claim a public source-kind spelling.

slots.name: ARITHMETIC_DISPATCH_ALIAS_INTEGER_SUBTRACT
slots.finding: Both dispatch tables point 002B to the same direct PSP/PS2 integer-subtract targets as 0009. The handler resolves a destination, collects one parameter, subtracts modulo 2^32, stores and returns native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: ARITHMETIC_DISPATCH_ALIAS_FLOAT_SUBTRACT
slots.finding: Both dispatch tables point 002C to the same direct PSP/PS2 float-subtract targets as 000A. The handler resolves a destination, collects one raw binary32 parameter, subtracts, stores and returns native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: ARITHMETIC_DISPATCH_ALIAS_INTEGER_MULTIPLY
slots.finding: Both dispatch tables point 002D to the same direct PSP/PS2 integer-multiply targets as 000B. The handler stores the low 32 product bits and returns native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: ARITHMETIC_DISPATCH_ALIAS_FLOAT_MULTIPLY
slots.finding: Both dispatch tables point 002E to the same direct PSP/PS2 float-multiply targets as 000C. The handler resolves a destination, collects one raw binary32 parameter, multiplies, stores and returns native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: ARITHMETIC_DISPATCH_ALIAS_INTEGER_DIVIDE
slots.finding: Both dispatch tables point 002F to the same direct PSP/PS2 integer-divide targets as 000D. The normal signed div/mflo path returns native status 0 (`CONTINUE`); zero-divisor and INT_MIN/-1 remain explicitly faulted portable boundaries.

slots.name: ARITHMETIC_DISPATCH_ALIAS_FLOAT_DIVIDE
slots.finding: Both dispatch tables point 0030 to the same direct PSP/PS2 float-divide targets as 000E. The handler resolves a destination, collects one raw binary32 parameter, divides, stores and returns native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: ADD_TIMED_FLOAT_PARAMETER_TO_FLOAT_VARIABLE
slots.finding: PSP/PS2 exact shared target pair: resolve one destination, collect one raw binary32 parameter, multiply by the engine frame-time scalar, add and store; native status 0 (`CONTINUE`). 0031/0032 share this target on both platforms, so no distinct public source-kind ABI is claimed.

slots.name: ADD_TIMED_FLOAT_VARIABLE_TO_FLOAT_VARIABLE
slots.finding: Exact dispatch alias of 0031 on PSP and PS2. Shared target resolves one destination, collects one raw binary32 parameter, adds parameter * engine frame-time scalar, stores and returns 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: SUB_TIMED_FLOAT_PARAMETER_FROM_FLOAT_VARIABLE
slots.finding: PSP/PS2 exact shared target pair: resolve one destination, collect one raw binary32 parameter, multiply by the engine frame-time scalar, subtract and store; native status 0 (`CONTINUE`). 0033/0034 share this target on both platforms, so no distinct public source-kind ABI is claimed.

slots.name: SUB_TIMED_FLOAT_VARIABLE_FROM_FLOAT_VARIABLE
slots.finding: Exact dispatch alias of 0033 on PSP and PS2. Shared target resolves one destination, collects one raw binary32 parameter, subtracts parameter * engine frame-time scalar, stores and returns 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: SET_VAR_INT_TO_VAR_INT
slots.finding: Shares the PSP/PS2 raw-dword assignment handler with 0004/0005/0036; PS2 directly stores the one collected parameter unchanged.

slots.name: SET_VAR_FLOAT_TO_VAR_FLOAT
slots.finding: Shares the PSP/PS2 raw-dword assignment handler with 0004/0005/0035; PS2 directly stores the one collected parameter unchanged.

slots.name: SET_VAR_TEXT_LABEL_TO_VAR_TEXT_LABEL
slots.finding: Both PSP and PS2 dispatch tables point 0037 to the exact same native target as 0006. The already reviewed shared handler resolves a destination, collects one raw dword, stores it, and returns native status 0 (`CONTINUE`). This confirms the target role; it does not invent a host string-pointer ABI.

slots.name: CSET_VAR_INT_TO_VAR_FLOAT
slots.finding: Both handlers resolve destination then source variables, convert source binary32 through native truncation toward zero and store int32; native status is 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: CSET_VAR_FLOAT_TO_VAR_INT
slots.finding: Both handlers resolve destination then source variables, convert source int32 through native binary32 conversion and store its raw float dword; native status is 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: ABS_INT
slots.finding: Both handlers conditionally negate one int32 variable with modulo-2^32 semantics; INT_MIN remains INT_MIN. Native status is 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: ABS_FLOAT
slots.finding: Both handlers negate one binary32 variable only when it is strictly less than +0.0, preserving -0 and unordered NaN input bits; native status is 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: IS_CHAR_STILL_ALIVE
slots.finding: Both handlers collect one character handle, evaluate an engine pool/state predicate, apply raw NOT at thread+0x20C, run the proven shared condition reducer at +0x206/+0x209 and return status 0 (`CONTINUE`). Pool layout and liveness predicate remain host-provided.

slots.name: CHARACTER_COORDINATE_PLACEMENT_BRIDGE
slots.finding: Both handlers collect exactly a character handle plus x/y/z binary32 payloads, resolve the character, and for z == -100.0 or z <= -250.0 replace z through a native ground-height query before the engine coordinate-placement path. Both return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: VEHICLE_DELETE_BRIDGE
slots.finding: Both handlers collect exactly one raw parameter, pass it to an engine vehicle-pool lookup, conditionally enter a native cleanup path when thread byte +0x20A is nonzero, then for a non-null entity remove it, remove its references and invoke the final virtual destruction path. Both return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: RETURN_TRUE
slots.finding: Both handlers apply the shared condition reducer with base predicate true (therefore respecting raw NOT), then call the shared return core; native status is 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: CLEAR_PRINTS_BRIDGE
slots.finding: Both handlers consume no SCM parameters, invoke one native UI/print clear callee and return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: RETURN_FALSE
slots.finding: Both handlers apply the shared condition reducer with base predicate false (therefore respecting raw NOT), then call the shared return core; native status is 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: IF
slots.finding: Both platforms collect one count, store uint16(count) at thread+0x206 and, for nonzero values, seed thread+0x209 true for counts <9 or false for counts >=9; native status is 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: LAUNCH_MISSION
slots.finding: Both handlers collect exactly one mission ID, pass ScriptParams[0] to an engine resolver, write byte one at +0x20A of the returned target script object, and return 0 (`CONTINUE`). Resolver lookup, target lifetime and service timing are host-owned.

slots.name: IS_BUTTON_PRESSED
slots.finding: Both handlers collect exactly two parameters, truncate ScriptParams[0]/[1] to uint16 in source order for one engine input predicate, then apply raw NOT and the shared +0x206/+0x209 condition reducer before returning 0 (`CONTINUE`). Meanings of the two narrowed inputs remain host-owned.

slots.name: SET_FADING_COLOUR
slots.finding: Both handlers collect three dwords, narrow each to low uint8 and invoke the fixed fade-subsystem colour method, then return status 0 (`CONTINUE`). Renderer state is host-provided.

slots.name: DO_FADE
slots.finding: Both handlers collect two dwords, map first <=2 to 0.0f otherwise float*0.001f, sign-narrow second to int16, invoke fixed fade start and return status 0 (`CONTINUE`). Mode meaning remains host-provided.

slots.name: GET_FADING_STATUS
slots.finding: Both handlers collect no SCM parameters, query fixed fade status, apply raw NOT at +0x20C and the exact shared +0x206/+0x209 condition reducer, then return status 0 (`CONTINUE`). Status probe is host-provided.

slots.name: PLAYER_STATE_CODE_TWO_CONDITION
slots.finding: Both handlers collect one raw player selector, resolve a host player object, compare its recovered state byte to literal 2, apply raw NOT at thread+0x20C and the exact common condition reducer at +0x206/+0x209, then return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: CHARACTER_DEAD_CONDITION
slots.finding: Both handlers collect one raw character handle, evaluate the same multi-branch engine predicate (null handle true; otherwise object-type/status checks including constants 1, 0x26, 0x39 and 0x3A), apply raw NOT at thread+0x20C and the exact common condition reducer, then return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: GET_GAME_TIMER
slots.finding: Both handlers copy the shared game-clock raw dword into ScriptParams[0], call StoreParameters with count 1 to consume one output destination, and return status 0 (`CONTINUE`). This is a script output, not an SCM return value.

slots.name: PLAYER_CONTROL_BRIDGE
slots.finding: Both handlers collect exactly two raw parameters, resolve parameter[0] through a player-table path, branch only on whether parameter[1] is zero, perform the platform player safety/camera/reset sequence and return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: VEHICLE_RELEASE_MARK_BRIDGE
slots.finding: Both handlers collect exactly one raw vehicle handle, resolve it through a vehicle-pool path, invoke a distinct vehicle release-mark helper and, only when thread byte +0x20A is nonzero, enter an additional context-cleanup path. Both return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`). This is not the destructive 0049 vehicle-delete path.

slots.name: GOSUB_FILE
slots.finding: Both native handlers collect exactly two parameters, push the post-parameter IP as a tagless frame at thread+0x14 indexed by thread+0x204, replace IP with collected parameter[0], and return status 0 (`CONTINUE`). Parameter[1] is consumed but not reread by either handler; no file-loader meaning is asserted.

slots.name: DISPLAY_TEXT
slots.finding: Both handlers collect two raw coordinate dwords, separately collect one raw text-key/offset dword, resolve it through platform text state, enqueue bounded UTF-16 display text and return 0 (`CONTINUE`). GXT lookup, text queue and rendering are host integration boundaries.

slots.name: SCRIPT_NAME
slots.finding: Both handlers collect one pointer-like parameter, copy exactly eight bytes with native strncpy semantics into thread+0x20F, lowercase only ASCII A..Z in all eight field positions, and return 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: CLEAR_HELP
slots.finding: Both handlers consume no SCM parameters, ensure their help/HUD manager exists, invoke two native clear paths and return 0 (`CONTINUE`). The PS2 second internal call has one additional constant flag whose meaning remains unasserted.

slots.name: LOAD_AND_LAUNCH_MISSION_INTERNAL
slots.finding: Both handlers collect one selector; in host mission mode they no-op below 0xFFFE or map selector to 0xFFFF-selector; then both stream a table-selected code slice, create a target script, set target bytes +0x20A/+0x217 and a global request byte, update mission context, immediately Process(target), and return 0 (`CONTINUE`). Streaming tables, buffers, factory, field meanings and scheduling boundary remain unimplemented host work.

slots.name: IS_INT_VAR_EQUAL_TO_CONSTANT
slots.finding: Shares the complete PSP/PS2 equality handler with 001B: it consumes two raw parameters, computes equality, applies raw NOT and the common condition reducer, then returns native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: SET_VAR_INT_TO_CONSTANT
slots.finding: Both tables share the 0004 raw assignment target: PSP has resolver/one-parameter collector setup and PS2 directly stores the collected dword unchanged.

slots.name: GET_PAD_STATE
slots.finding: Both handlers collect one selector, use a native unsigned 0..44 pad-accessor dispatch to overwrite ScriptParams[0] only in range, then StoreParameters(1) into one output destination and return 0 (`CONTINUE`). Out-of-range selector is stored unchanged; in-range input state is host-provided.

slots.name: CALL_NOT
slots.finding: Both platforms enter the common CALL handler, compare the preserved opcode with 0x037B, push a thread+0x204 call-frame entry, consume call metadata/arguments and report native VM dispatch status 0 (`CONTINUE`). The non-0x037B branch uses the CALL_NOT frame tag (0x00c00000).

slots.name: CALL
slots.finding: Both platforms use the same handler as 0x037A, but the `opcode == 0x037B` branch writes the distinct CALL frame tag (0x00800000) before collecting call metadata/arguments and reports native VM dispatch status 0 (`CONTINUE`). This proves the shared target is not an accidental table alias.

slots.name: DISABLE_PAUSE_MENU
slots.finding: Both handlers collect exactly one raw parameter, reduce it only to zero/non-zero, forward false/true to their native pause-menu setter path, and return 0 (`CONTINUE`). The menu object's lifetime and host application remain outside the VM.

slots.name: IS_THIS_SCRIPT_A_MISSION
slots.finding: Both handlers read byte +0x217 from the VM global active-script object, apply the dispatcher's raw NOT and the exact shared +0x206/+0x209 condition reducer, then return 0 (`CONTINUE`). No SCM parameters are consumed.

slots.name: GLOBAL_BYTE_STORE_BRIDGE
slots.finding: Both handlers collect exactly two raw parameters, calculate an address in a fixed engine-global byte region from parameter[0], store only the low byte of parameter[1], and return native status 0 (`CONTINUE`).

slots.name: COMMAND_055A
slots.finding: Both zero-parameter handlers prove the same full reducer: base engine predicate XOR thread+0x20c; state 0 assigns thread+0x209; old states <9 decrement and AND; old states >=9 decrement and OR, then clear thread+0x206 if its decremented value is <0x15; native VM dispatch status 0 (`CONTINUE`). The public opcode list provides no semantic name, so a generic name is retained.
